elements.text: Rosie the Riveter represents the American women who helped the United States win World War II.

contents.text: In the 1910s, San Francisco was growing quickly. People were beginning to buy cars. But they still needed ferry boats to cross San Francisco Bay. Using the ferry could take a long time.
Some people wanted to build a bridge across the Golden Gate. But the strait was over a mile wide! No bridges in the United States were that long.

subpoints.text: People began to think seriously about building a bridge in 1919. Engineers worked together to come up with plan for the bridge. It needed to be strong enough to stand up to the strong winds and powerful waters of the bay. Designers also thought about how to make the bridge beautiful. After years of work, the Golden Gate Bridge opened in 1937.

explanationText.text: Some people worried that the rocks under the water would not support the bridge. If the bridge fell, it could hurt people and block the bay. The United States War Department also worried that enemies could attack the bridge.

explanationText.text: The Golden Gate gave a beautiful view out to the ocean. People worried that adding something man-made would make the area less beautiful.

content.text: Some people worried that ferry boat companies would lose money.

explanationText.text: Before the Golden Gate Bridge, people used ferry boats to cross the water. With a bridge, people would be able to walk or drive instead. They would spend less money on ferry rides.

subpoints.text: People began to think seriously about building a bridge in 1919. Engineers worked together to come up with plan for the bridge. It needed to be strong enough to stand up to the strong winds and powerful waters of the bay. Designers also thought about how to make the bridge beautiful. After years of work, the Golden Gate Bridge opened in 1937.

is something that is built to honor a person or an event.

contents.text: Work on Mount Rushmore started in the 1920s. By that time, the United States was about 150 years old. The presidents on the monument were meant to stand for important moments in those 150 years. The table below shows what each president represents:

table.text: George Washington helped form the United States. He led the Patriots through the Revolutionary War. Later, he became the country's first president.
growing the country toward the West
As president, Thomas Jefferson made the United States much larger. He added land from the Mississippi River to the Rocky Mountains. He also sent Lewis and Clark to explore the new land.
keeping the country together through the Civil War
Abraham Lincoln led the country through the Civil War. The war tested whether or not the United States could stay together.
growing the country into a great power
Theodore Roosevelt was president at the beginning of the 20th century. He helped make the United States one of the most powerful countries in the world.

subheader.text: Why wasn't there enough money to finish Mount Rushmore?

subpoints.text: Most of the money had been coming from the federal government. But by 1941, the United States was getting ready for war. The United States joined World War II in December 1941.
The government needed money for the war. So, it stopped paying for the Mount Rushmore monument.

contents.text: Work on Mount Rushmore started in the 1920s. By that time, the United States was about 150 years old. The presidents on the monument were meant to stand for important moments in those 150 years. The table below shows what each president represents:

table.text: George Washington helped form the United States. He led the Patriots through the Revolutionary War. Later, he became the country's first president.
growing the country toward the West
As president, Thomas Jefferson made the United States much larger. He added land from the Mississippi River to the Rocky Mountains. He also sent Lewis and Clark to explore the new land.
keeping the country together through the Civil War
Abraham Lincoln led the country through the Civil War. The war tested whether or not the United States could stay together.
growing the country into a great power
Theodore Roosevelt was president at the beginning of the 20th century. He helped make the United States one of the most powerful countries in the world.

subheader.text: Where did the idea for Mount Rushmore come from?

subpoints.text: The idea for Mount Rushmore came from South Dakota's state historian. He wanted to bring more visitors to the state. So, he came up with an idea for a monument  celebrating heroes from the West. It would honor Native American men like Red Cloud and white men like Lewis and Clark.
The historian found an artist named Gutzon Borglum  to design the monument. However, the artist  had a different idea. He said that more people would come to see the presidents.

contents.text: When did workers start carving Mount Rushmore?
When did workers start carving Mount Rushmore?

Work on Mount Rushmore began earlier in the 1920s. In 1923, the state historian of South Dakota came up with the idea for a large monument. He hoped that it would bring visitors to the area. He found an artist, and work began in 1927.
Sometimes work on Mount Rushmore went quickly, and sometimes there were long breaks. Work finally ended in 1941, 14 years after it started.
